channel.title: Wire — DevOps
channel.description: DevOps from thirty sources, one digest a day.

item.title: You Can’t Have a Rollback Button
item.description: I’ve worked with deploy systems in the past that have a prominent “rollback” button, or a console incantation with the same effect. The presence of one of these is reassuring, in that you can imagine… (1 source: sreweekly)

item.title: Rollback Does Not Erase Distributed Memory
Atlassian Rebuilds Metrics Pipeline Around OpenTelemetry at Massive Scale
item.description: Software company Atlassian has published an account of its migration from gostatsd to OpenTelemetry, replacing the internal workings of a metrics platform that receives data from about 100,000 hosts across 14 regions. (1 source: infoq)

item.title: Kubernetes Teams Get a Safer Way to See Their Own GPU Metrics
item.description: Adobe engineers have described an open-source approach for giving teams self-service access to their own Prometheus metrics in multi-tenant Kubernetes environments, without exposing the shared metrics of other teams. By Craig Risi (1 source: infoq)

item.title: Cloudflare Worker Previews: Per-Branch Environments for Workers
item.description: Cloudflare has introduced Worker Previews. This feature allows each Git branch to have its own isolated, production-like environment for a Worker. Each environment has a stable URL. (1 source: infoq)

item.title: The architecture of Neki
item.description: Sharded Postgres, from the team behind Vitess (1 source: sreweekly)
